sanskrit: nākampata mahābāhuḥ svadhairyaṃ samupāśritaḥ sāyakāṃś caiva vividhān aśvatthāmni mumoca ha
english: The mighty-armed one did not waver, resting upon his own steadfastness, and he loosed manifold arrows upon Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: tau punaḥ saṃnyavartetāṃ prāṇadyūtapare raṇe nivārayantau bāṇaughaiḥ parasparam amarṣiṇau utsṛjantau maheṣvāsau śaravṛṣṭīḥ samantataḥ
english: Once more the two turned back to the battle in which life itself was the wager, those two unforgiving great archers warding off each other with floods of arrows, pouring forth showers of shafts on every side.

sanskrit: drauṇipārṣatayor yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam dṛṣṭvā saṃpūjayām āsuḥ siddhacāraṇavātikāḥ
english: Beholding the dreadful and terrifying combat of the son of Droṇa and the son of Pṛṣata, the bands of Siddhas and Cāraṇas honored it with praise.

sanskrit: śaraughaiḥ pūrayantau tāv ākāśaṃ pradiśas tathā alakṣyau samayudhyetāṃ mahat kṛtvā śarais tamaḥ
english: Filling the sky and the quarters with their floods of arrows, the two fought unseen, having wrought a great darkness with their shafts.

sanskrit: nṛtyamānāv iva raṇe maṇḍalīkṛtakārmukau parasparavadhe yattau parasparajayaiṣiṇau
english: As though dancing in the fray, their bows drawn into perfect circles, each strove to slay the other, each longing to vanquish the other.

sanskrit: ayudhyetāṃ mahābāhū citraṃ laghu ca suṣṭhu ca saṃpūjyamānau samare yodhamukhyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: The two mighty-armed warriors fought with skill, with swiftness, and with mastery, honored in the battle by thousands of the foremost fighters.

sanskrit: tau prayuddhau raṇe dṛṣṭvā vane vanyau gajāv iva ubhayoḥ senayor harṣas tumulaḥ samapadyata
english: Seeing the two locked in combat in the fray like two wild elephants in the forest, a tumultuous joy arose in both armies.

sanskrit: siṃhanādaravāś cāsan dadhmuḥ śaṅkhāṃś ca māriṣa vāditrāṇy abhyavādyanta śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: There were roars like the lion's roar, and they blew their conches, O honored one, and instruments were sounded by the hundreds and the thousands.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu tumule yuddhe bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhane muhūrtam iva tad yuddhaṃ samarūpaṃ tadābhavat
english: In that tumultuous battle, which swelled the terror of the timid, the combat for a moment then stood evenly matched.

sanskrit: tato drauṇir mahārāja pārṣatasya mahātmanaḥ dhvajaṃ dhanus tathā chatram ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī sūtam aśvāṃś ca caturo nihatyābhyadravad raṇe
english: Then, O great king, the son of Droṇa, having struck down the banner, the bow, the parasol, both the flank-guarding charioteers, the driver, and the four horses of the high-souled son of Pṛṣata, charged upon him in the fray.

sanskrit: pāñcālāṃś caiva tān sarvān bāṇaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ vyadrāvayad ameyātmā śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And all those Pāñcālas the immeasurable-souled one routed by the hundreds and the thousands with his straight-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravivyathe senā pāṇḍavī bharatarṣabha dṛṣṭvā drauṇer mahat karma vāsavasyeva saṃyuge
english: Then the army of the Pāṇḍavas trembled, O bull of the Bhāratas, beholding the mighty feat of Droṇa's son, like that of Vāsava in battle.

sanskrit: śatena ca śataṃ hatvā pāñcālānāṃ mahārathaḥ tribhiś ca niśitair bāṇair hatvā trīn vai mahārathān
english: Slaying a hundred of the Pāñcālas with a hundred shafts, the great chariot-warrior, and with three sharp arrows slaying three great chariot-warriors,

sanskrit: drauṇir drupadaputrasya phalgunasya ca paśyataḥ nāśayām āsa pāñcālān bhūyiṣṭhaṃ ye vyavasthitāḥ
english: the son of Droṇa, before the very eyes of Drupada's son and of Phalguna, destroyed the greater part of the Pāñcālas who stood their ground.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ pāñcālāḥ samare saha sṛñjayaiḥ agacchan drauṇim utsṛjya viprakīrṇarathadhvajāḥ
english: Those Pāñcālas, being slaughtered in the battle together with the Sṛñjayas, fled, abandoning the son of Droṇa, their chariots and banners scattered.

sanskrit: sa jitvā samare śatrūn droṇaputro mahārathaḥ nanāda sumahānādaṃ tapānte jalado yathā
english: Having conquered his foes in the battle, the son of Droṇa, that great chariot-warrior, roared a mighty roar, like a thundercloud at the close of the hot season.

sanskrit: sa nihatya bahūñ śūrān aśvatthāmā vyarocata yugānte sarvabhūtāni bhasma kṛtveva pāvakaḥ
english: Having slain many heroes, Aśvatthāman shone forth like the fire that reduces all beings to ashes at the end of an age.

sanskrit: saṃpūjyamāno yudhi kauraveyair; vijitya saṃkhye 'rigaṇān sahasraśaḥ vyarocata droṇasutaḥ pratāpavān; yathā surendro 'rigaṇān nihatya
english: Honored in the battle by the Kauravas, having vanquished hosts of foes by the thousands, the valiant son of Droṇa shone forth like the lord of the gods after slaying the hosts of his enemies.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiraś caiva bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ droṇaputraṃ mahārāja samantāt paryavārayan
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Yudhiṣṭhira and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, O great king, surrounded the son of Droṇa on every side.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā bhāradvājena saṃvṛtaḥ abhyayāt pāṇḍavān saṃkhye tato yuddham avartata ghorarūpaṃ mahārāja bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhanam
english: Then King Duryodhana, guarded by the son of Bharadvāja, advanced upon the Pāṇḍavas in battle, and thereupon a combat ensued, dreadful in aspect, O great king, swelling the terror of the timid.

sanskrit: ambaṣṭhān mālavān vaṅgāñ śibīṃs traigartakān api prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya gaṇān kruddho yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: The Ambaṣṭhas, the Mālavas, the Vaṅgas, the Śibis, and the Traigartas as well — those bands the wrathful Yudhiṣṭhira dispatched to the realm of Death.

sanskrit: abhīṣāhāñ śūrasenān kṣatriyān yuddhadurmadān nikṛtya pṛthivīṃ cakre bhīmaḥ śoṇitakardamām
english: Cutting down the Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, and the Kṣatriyas frenzied for war, Bhīma made the earth a mire of blood.

sanskrit: yaudheyāraṭṭarājanyān madrakāṃś ca gaṇān yudhi prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya kirīṭī niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The Yaudheyas, the Āraṭṭas, the princes, and the bands of Madrakas in the battle the Diademed One dispatched to the realm of Death with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: pragāḍham añjogatibhir nārācair abhipīḍitāḥ nipetur dviradā bhūmau dviśṛṅgā iva parvatāḥ
english: Sorely afflicted by straight-flying iron shafts driven deep, the elephants fell to the earth like two-peaked mountains.

sanskrit: nikṛttair hastihastaiś ca luṭhamānais tatas tataḥ rarāja vasudhā kīrṇā visarpadbhir ivoragaiḥ
english: With the severed trunks of elephants writhing here and there, the earth, strewn with them, glowed as though covered with gliding serpents.

sanskrit: kṣiptaiḥ kanakacitraiś ca nṛpacchatraiḥ kṣitir babhau dyaur ivādityacandrādyair grahaiḥ kīrṇā yugakṣaye
english: With the cast-down royal parasols, bright with gold, the earth shone like the sky strewn with the sun, the moon, and the other heavenly bodies at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: hata praharatābhītā vidhyata vyavakṛntata ity āsīt tumulaḥ śabdaḥ śoṇāśvasya rathaṃ prati
english: "Slay! Strike without fear! Pierce! Cut them down!" — such was the tumultuous cry around the chariot of him whose horses were red.

sanskrit: droṇas tu paramakruddho vāyavyāstreṇa saṃyuge vyadhamat tān yathā vāyur meghān iva duratyayaḥ
english: But Droṇa, exceedingly enraged, with the Wind-weapon in the battle scattered them, as the irresistible wind scatters the clouds.

sanskrit: te hanyamānā droṇena pāñcālāḥ prādravan bhayāt paśyato bhīmasenasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Those Pāñcālas, being slain by Droṇa, fled in terror, even before the eyes of Bhīmasena and of the high-souled Pārtha.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭī bhīmaś ca sahasā saṃnyavartatām mahatā rathavaṃśena parigṛhya balaṃ tava
english: Then the Diademed One and Bhīma suddenly turned back, encircling thy host with a great array of chariots.

sanskrit: bībhatsur dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvam uttaraṃ tu vṛkodaraḥ bhāradvājaṃ śaraughābhyāṃ mahadbhyām abhyavarṣatām
english: Bībhatsu on the right flank and Vṛkodara on the north, the two rained upon the son of Bharadvāja with their two great floods of arrows.

sanskrit: tau tadā sṛñjayāś caiva pāñcālāś ca mahārathāḥ anvagacchan mahārāja matsyāś ca saha somakaiḥ
english: Then the Sṛñjayas and the Pāñcāla great chariot-warriors followed those two, O great king, and the Matsyas together with the Somakas.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava putrasya rathodārāḥ prahāriṇaḥ mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ jagmur droṇarathaṃ prati
english: Likewise the noble car-warriors and strikers of thy son advanced with a great host toward the chariot of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā bharatī senā vadhyamānā kirīṭinā tamasā nidrayā caiva punar eva vyadīryata
english: Then that Bhārata army, being slaughtered by the Diademed One, and overcome by darkness and by sleep, was again torn asunder.

sanskrit: droṇena vāryamāṇās te svayaṃ tava sutena ca na śakyante mahārāja yodhā vārayituṃ tadā
english: Though held back by Droṇa and by thy son himself, the warriors could not then be restrained, O great king.

sanskrit: sā pāṇḍuputrasya śarair dāryamāṇā mahācamūḥ tamasā saṃvṛte loke vyadravat sarvatomukhī
english: That great army, rent by the arrows of the son of Pāṇḍu, fled in all directions as the world was wrapped in darkness.

sanskrit: utsṛjya śataśo vāhāṃs tatra ke cin narādhipāḥ prādravanta mahārāja bhayāviṣṭāḥ samantataḥ
english: Abandoning their mounts by the hundreds, some of the kings there fled, O great king, seized with terror on every side.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca somadattaṃ tu saṃprekṣya vidhunvānaṃ mahad dhanuḥ sātyakiḥ prāha yantāraṃ somadattāya māṃ vaha
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding Somadatta brandishing his mighty bow, Sātyaki said to his charioteer, "Bear me toward Somadatta.

sanskrit: na hy ahatvā raṇe śatruṃ bāhlīkaṃ kauravādhamam nivartiṣye raṇāt sūta satyam etad vaco mama
english: For without slaying in the fray my foe, the Bāhlīka, basest of the Kauravas, I will not turn back from the battle, O charioteer — this word of mine is true."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpreṣayad yantā saindhavāṃs tān mahājavān turaṅgamāñ śaṅkhavarṇān sarvaśabdātigān raṇe
english: Then the driver urged on those swift Saindhava steeds, conch-colored, outstripping every sound in the battle.

sanskrit: te 'vahan yuyudhānaṃ tu manomārutaraṃhasaḥ yathendraṃ harayo rājan purā daityavadhodyatam
english: With the speed of thought and of the wind, they bore Yuyudhāna, O king, as of old the tawny steeds bore Indra when he set out to slay the Daityas.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya sātvataṃ rabhasaṃ raṇe somadatto mahābāhur asaṃbhrānto 'bhyavartata
english: Seeing the impetuous Sātvata rushing upon him in the fray, the mighty-armed Somadatta, undismayed, advanced to meet him.

sanskrit: vimuñcañ śaravarṣāṇi parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān chādayām āsa śaineyaṃ jalado bhāskaraṃ yathā
english: Loosing showers of arrows like a rain-laden storm-cloud, he covered the grandson of Śini, as a cloud covers the sun.

sanskrit: asaṃbhrāntaś ca samare sātyakiḥ kurupuṃgavam chādayām āsa bāṇaughaiḥ samantād bharatarṣabha
english: And undismayed in the battle, Sātyaki covered that bull of the Kurus on every side with floods of arrows, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: somadattas tu taṃ ṣaṣṭyā vivyādhorasi mādhavam sātyakiś cāpi taṃ rājann avidhyat sāyakaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: Somadatta pierced that Mādhava in the breast with sixty shafts, and Sātyaki too, O king, struck him with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ śaraiḥ kṛttau vyarājetāṃ nararṣabhau supuṣpau puṣpasamaye puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Those two bulls among men, gashed by each other's arrows, shone like two kiṃśuka trees in fair flower at the flowering season.

sanskrit: rudhirokṣitasarvāṅgau kuruvṛṣṇiyaśaskarau parasparam avekṣetāṃ dahantāv iva locanaiḥ
english: Their every limb drenched with blood, those bringers of glory to the Kurus and the Vṛṣṇis gazed upon each other as though scorching one another with their eyes.

sanskrit: rathamaṇḍalamārgeṣu carantāv arimardanau ghorarūpau hi tāv āstāṃ vṛṣṭimantāv ivāmbudau
english: Ranging along the circling paths of their chariots, those two crushers of foes were of dreadful aspect, like two rain-laden clouds.

sanskrit: śarasaṃbhinnagātrau tau sarvataḥ śakalīkṛtau śvāvidhāv iva rājendra vyadṛṣyetāṃ śarakṣatau
english: Their bodies pierced through by arrows, bristling on all sides, wounded by shafts, they appeared, O lord of kings, like two porcupines.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhair iṣubhir ācitau tau vyarocatām khadyotair āvṛtau rājan prāvṛṣīva vanaspatī
english: Studded with gold-feathered arrows, the two shone forth, O king, like two forest trees covered with fireflies in the rains.

sanskrit: saṃpradīpitasarvāṅgau sāyakais tau mahārathau adṛśyetāṃ raṇe kruddhāv ulkābhir iva kuñjarau
english: Their every limb set ablaze, as it were, by arrows, those two great chariot-warriors appeared in the fray, wrathful, like two elephants amid firebrands.

sanskrit: tato yudhi mahārāja somadatto mahārathaḥ ardhacandreṇa ciccheda mādhavasya mahad dhanuḥ
english: Then in the battle, O great king, Somadatta the great chariot-warrior, with a crescent-headed arrow, cut asunder the mighty bow of the Mādhava.

sanskrit: athainaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā sāyakānāṃ samārpayat tvaramāṇas tvarākāle punaś ca daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then he assailed him with twenty-five arrows, and, making haste at the hour for haste, with ten more shafts.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sātyakir vegavattaram pañcabhiḥ sāyakais tūrṇaṃ somadattam avidhyata
english: Then, taking up another, swifter bow, Sātyaki quickly pierced Somadatta with five arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa bhallena dhvajaṃ ciccheda kāñcanam bāhlīkasya raṇe rājan sātyakiḥ prahasann iva
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft Sātyaki cut down the golden banner of the Bāhlīka in the fray, O king, as though smiling.

sanskrit: somadattas tv asaṃbhrānto dṛṣṭvā ketuṃ nipātitam śaineyaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā sāyakānāṃ samācinot
english: But Somadatta, undismayed, seeing his standard struck down, covered the grandson of Śini with twenty-five arrows.

sanskrit: sātvato 'pi raṇe kruddhaḥ somadattasya dhanvinaḥ dhanuś ciccheda samare kṣurapreṇa śitena ha
english: The Sātvata too, enraged in the battle, with a sharp razor-edged arrow cut asunder the bow of the bowman Somadatta in the fray.

sanskrit: athainaṃ rukmapuṅkhānāṃ śatena nataparvaṇām ācinod bahudhā rājan bhagnadaṃṣṭram iva dvipam
english: Then he covered him in many places with a hundred straight-jointed, gold-feathered arrows, O king, like an elephant with a broken tusk.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya somadatto mahārathaḥ sātyakiṃ chādayām āsa śaravṛṣṭyā mahābalaḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, the mighty Somadatta, that great chariot-warrior, covered Sātyaki with a shower of arrows.

sanskrit: somadattaṃ tu saṃkruddho raṇe vivyādha sātyakiḥ sātyakiṃ ceṣujālena somadatto apīḍayat
english: But the wrathful Sātyaki pierced Somadatta in the fray, and Somadatta in turn afflicted Sātyaki with a net of arrows.

sanskrit: daśabhiḥ sātvatasyārthe bhīmo 'han bāhlikātmajam somadatto 'py asaṃbhrāntaḥ śaineyam avadhīc charaiḥ
english: For the Sātvata's sake Bhīma struck the son of Bāhlika with ten arrows, and Somadatta too, undismayed, smote the grandson of Śini with shafts.

sanskrit: tatas tu sātvatasyārthe bhaimasenir navaṃ dṛḍham mumoca parighaṃ ghoraṃ somadattasya vakṣasi
english: Then for the Sātvata's sake the son of Bhīmasena hurled a new, stout, and dreadful iron club at the breast of Somadatta.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena parighaṃ ghoradarśanam dvidhā ciccheda samare prahasann iva kauravaḥ
english: That iron club of terrible aspect, rushing on with speed, the Kaurava cut in two in the fray, as though smiling.

sanskrit: sa papāta dvidhā chinna āyasaḥ parigho mahān mahīdharasyeva mahac chikharaṃ vajradāritam
english: That great iron club, cleft in two, fell down like the great peak of a mountain riven by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tatas tu sātyakī rājan somadattasya saṃyuge dhanuś ciccheda bhallena hastāvāpaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ
english: Then Sātyaki, O king, in the combat cut asunder Somadatta's bow with a broad-headed shaft, and his leather glove with five arrows.

sanskrit: caturbhis tu śarais tūrṇaṃ caturas turagottamān samīpaṃ preṣayām āsa pretarājasya bhārata
english: And with four arrows he swiftly dispatched the four excellent steeds to the presence of the king of the dead, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sāratheś ca śiraḥ kāyād bhallena nataparvaṇā jahāra rathaśārdūlaḥ prahasañ śinipuṃgavaḥ
english: And with a straight-jointed broad-headed shaft that tiger among chariot-warriors, the bull of Śini's line, smiling, severed the charioteer's head from his body.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraṃ mahāghoraṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam mumoca sātvato rājan svarṇapuṅkhaṃ śilāśitam
english: Then the Sātvata loosed a most terrible arrow, blazing like fire, gold-feathered and whetted on stone, O king.

sanskrit: sa vimukto balavatā śaineyena śarottamaḥ ghoras tasyorasi vibho nipapātāśu bhārata
english: That excellent shaft, loosed by the mighty grandson of Śini, dreadful, fell swiftly upon his breast, O lord, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā sātvatena mahārathaḥ somadatto mahābāhur nipapāta mamāra ca
english: Sorely pierced by the mighty Sātvata, that great chariot-warrior, the mighty-armed Somadatta, fell down and died.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ tatra somadattaṃ mahārathāḥ mahatā śaravarṣeṇa yuyudhānam upādravan
english: Seeing Somadatta slain there, the great chariot-warriors rushed upon Yuyudhāna with a great shower of arrows.

sanskrit: chādyamānaṃ śarair dṛṣṭvā yuyudhānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ droṇānīkam upādravat
english: Seeing Yuyudhāna being overwhelmed with arrows, Yudhiṣṭhira, with a great host, charged upon Droṇa's array.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kruddhas tāvakānāṃ mahābalam śarair vidrāvayām āsa bhāradvājasya paśyataḥ
english: Then the wrathful Yudhiṣṭhira routed with his arrows the mighty force of thy men, before the very eyes of the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: sainyāni drāvayantaṃ tu droṇo dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiram abhidudrāva vegena krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
english: But Droṇa, seeing Yudhiṣṭhira putting his troops to flight, rushed upon him with speed, his eyes reddened with wrath.

sanskrit: tataḥ suniśitair bāṇaiḥ pārthaṃ vivyādha saptabhiḥ so 'tividdho mahābāhuḥ sṛkkiṇī parisaṃlihan yudhiṣṭhirasya ciccheda dhvajaṃ kārmukam eva ca
english: Then with seven well-sharpened arrows he pierced the Pārtha; and, sorely pierced himself, the mighty-armed one, licking the corners of his mouth, cut down Yudhiṣṭhira's banner and his bow as well.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā tvaritas tvarākāle nṛpottamaḥ anyad ādatta vegena kārmukaṃ samare dṛḍham
english: His bow severed, that best of kings, making haste at the hour for haste, quickly took up another stout bow in the fray.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa droṇaṃ vivyādha pārthivaḥ sāśvasūtadhvajarathaṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then the king pierced Droṇa, together with his horses, driver, banner, and chariot, with a thousand arrows; and that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtaṃ vyathitaḥ śaraghātaprapīḍitaḥ niṣasāda rathopasthe droṇo bharatasattama
english: Then for a moment, shaken and afflicted by the stroke of those arrows, Droṇa sank down upon the floor of his chariot, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ muhūrtād dvijasattamaḥ krodhena mahatāviṣṭo vāyavyāstram avāsṛjat
english: Then, regaining his senses in a moment, that best of the twice-born, seized with great wrath, loosed the Wind-weapon.

sanskrit: asaṃbhrāntas tataḥ pārtho dhanur ākṛṣya vīryavān tad astram astreṇa raṇe stambhayām āsa bhārata
english: Then the valiant Pārtha, undismayed, drawing his bow, checked that weapon with a weapon of his own in the fray, O Bhārata.
